walkthroughs.body_html:
New Testament Studies / Study of a World Religion — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

New Testament Studies / Study of a World Religion brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with New Testament Studies / Study of a World Religion.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

mcqs.q: What does the secularisation thesis claim?
options: Secularisation means everyone in modern countries is now atheist.
That as societies modernise, religion declines in social significance — though sociologists now debate this, since global religion has not declined uniformly.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Secularisation means the separation of church and state.
